round_goal: Restore the `/policy-lab` page to a non-500 response for anonymous harness visits without regressing the existing access-control contract, then re-run the harness to recover a third consecutive passing round.

priorities.title: Fix `/policy-lab` runtime failure
priorities.action: The current blocker is Tier 2 only: `harness/results/tier-2.json` shows both desktop and mobile `/policy-lab` checks failing with HTTP 500, and `harness/results/tier-2.server.err.log` identifies `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'HTTPException'` inside `policy_lab_page`. Remove the local import shadowing so the `except HTTPException` branch works, and keep the page serving `static/policy-lab.html` instead of crashing.

priorities.title: Preserve access control while making the route harness-safe
priorities.action: Do not weaken the intended gate. `policy_lab_page` should still attempt `require_admin(request)` first and then fall back to the existing allowed non-admin access path. The fix should only stop anonymous requests from turning into a server error; it should not remove the route's admin-first check or introduce new auth regressions.

priorities.title: Verify with targeted checks and the full harness
priorities.action: After the route fix, run the smallest relevant verification first, then the full harness loop command. Confirm `/policy-lab` no longer returns 500 in the UX harness, and let the evaluator update `harness/RESULTS.md` toward the required 3 consecutive passes.

generator_prompt: Focus on the `/policy-lab` failure. The latest evaluator state is: Tier 1 passing, Tier 3 passing, Tier 2 failing because `/policy-lab` returns HTTP 500 on both desktop and mobile. The server log points to `backend/policy_admin_routes.py` in `policy_lab_page`, where `except HTTPException:` is followed later by `from fastapi import HTTPException`, creating a local-name shadowing bug and raising `UnboundLocalError`. Fix that route so anonymous harness visits no longer crash the server and `static/policy-lab.html` is served normally. Preserve the existing admin-first access pattern: keep the `require_admin(request)` call and its fallback logic intact rather than deleting access checks. After editing, run targeted verification around the policy-lab route/tests, then run `.venv\Scripts\python.exe harness/scripts/run_all_harness.py --rounds 15` and use the new results to confirm Tier 2 is back to green.
